core_obligations: Write the rank of M over R as the dimension over K of M tensor K (proof line 5079).
Write the rank of M tensor R' over R' as the dimension over the fraction field K' of (M tensor R') tensor K' and identify this as the base change of M tensor K along K to K' (proof lines 5078-5080).
Apply invariance of dimension under extension of the ground field to conclude that the two ranks are equal (proof line 5080).

The nearest records are 336 (4721-4764, tag 0H7R) and 337 (5577-5633, tag 0AVB); this card is the short rank statement of the section on ranks of modules, which the published set does not contain at all.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for an extension of domains R inside R' the rank of an R-module M equals the rank of M tensor R' over R' (statement lines 5071-5075), and the author's proof identifies the reason in one sentence: dimension of a vector space is invariant under extension of the ground field (proof lines 5078-5080). What has to be seen is that the two ranks are two dimensions of two vector spaces over two different fields, K and the fraction field of R', and that the vector space for R' is the base change of the one for R along K to K', which is where the invariance applies. There is no computation left at the end of the proof; the content is the identification of the two dimensions.
